title: Tensorize: Fast Synthesis of Tensor Programs from Legacy Code using Symbolic Tracing, Sketching and Solving
problem: Achieving tensor DSL performance benefits for existing applications requires manual rewriting in evolving DSLs. Prior automatic translation approaches face significant scalability issues limiting applicability to real-world code.
motivation: Tensor DSLs unlock substantial performance through high-level compiler optimization and hardware acceleration, but programmer effort to migrate legacy code is prohibitive.
method: Tensorize automatically converts code to use tensor DSLs (specialized languages for efficient numerical operations) by creating a symbolic trace—a mathematical record of what the program does. It then finds equivalent patterns (sketches) from the target DSL and uses an algebraic solver (a tool that simplifies mathematical expressions) to transform these into the most efficient tensor form. Since the solver works by proven mathematical rules, the result is guaranteed to produce identical outputs to the original program.
key_novelty: Using an algebraic solver on symbolic program traces enables fast, provably-correct automatic translation to tensor DSLs.
contributions: MLIR-based program synthesis framework for tensor DSL lifting
Symbolic trace specification with automatic sketch selection
Algebraic solver for rapid specification simplification
Lifts more code than prior schemes, order of magnitude faster, guarantees correctness

metrics.speedup: Order of magnitude faster synthesis than prior schemes

baselines: Prior automatic tensor DSL translation approaches
limitations: Specific benchmark results and performance metrics not provided in abstract.
